intro: An average prediction treats underestimates and overestimates symmetrically. Quantile loss changes that balance to target a chosen part of a distribution.
task: Return the mean pinball loss and its per-prediction subgradient for a fixed quantile.
requirements: targets and predictions are equal-length vectors. quantile is a scalar in [0,1]. Let residual=target-prediction.
Each loss is quantile*residual for residual>=0 and (quantile-1)*residual for residual<0. Return {"loss": mean_loss, "gradient": per-prediction derivatives of that mean}.
Gradient entries are -quantile/n for positive residual, (1-quantile)/n for negative residual, and zero at exactly zero residual. Do not take a gradient with respect to targets.

Use real finite numeric inputs with magnitude at most 1e6, excluding booleans. Vectors have length 1..128 and matrix axes have length 1..128 unless a tighter bound is stated. Leave all inputs unchanged; raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

Asymmetric penalty
Overprediction

hints.title: Find the structure
hints.body: Split residuals by sign to distinguish underprediction from overprediction at the selected quantile.

hints.title: Build the calculation
hints.body: Differentiate with respect to predictions, which reverses the residual slope, and divide each derivative by sample count.

explanation: Underestimation and overestimation have different slopes. At a high quantile, an underestimate is penalized more strongly, shifting a fitted constant toward the upper part of the observations.
The reported vector differentiates the mean loss, so each component includes division by the observation count. At zero residual the loss has a kink and this exercise chooses the zero subgradient.
